newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Ahold unit welcomes Shell store deal.
newsitem.headline: Ahold unit welcomes Shell store deal.

text.p: Dutch supermarkets chain Albert Heijn is 'very happy' with the agreement reached with Shell to open small-scale shops at Shell service stations in the Netherlands, the Ahold subsidiary said on Wednesday.
"The agreement is a win-win situation which will benefit both companies and the Dutch consumer," Albert Heijn director Jan Andreae said in a statement.
As the exact number of outlets to be opened is still unclear, Albert Heijn could not give an indication of the expected additional turnover.
"We don't know the exact number of shops to be opened yet, but it will be several hundred. We'll look at each station and assess the possibilities," Albert Heijn spokesman Erik Muller told Reuters.
Earlier today, Shell and Ahold said Albert Heijn outlets would be opened at a "substantial number" of Shell's 750 or so Dutch service stations.
"Each location's possibilities have to be analysed, the shop has to be redesigned, ... I can't say how long it will take, but we'll do it at high speed," Muller said.
It would take some years to finalise the project, he said.
The stores' size will vary, but all will carry a range of some 1,000 products including dairy and fresh produce, he said.
Shell already operates another retail format, Select Convenience, at its pump stations.
It said the new Albert Heijn outlets, which it will operate under a franchise agreement with the Ahold subsidiary, would be integrated into the existing retail network.
The companies started the partnership experiment in March 1995, opening four small Albert Heijn outlets at Shell service stations in three cities.
"The stores...complement our nationwide network and clearly cater to customers' needs also to shop out of hours and at other than conventional retail outlets," Jan Andreae said.
